subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@brightdesk.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Hi Samir / Ava —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and the next steps we discussed so everyone has the same view. Please correct anything I missed.

Key pain points you outlined:
- Cost volatility and rising per-token spend on OpenAI / Anthropic for high-volume chat and embedding workloads.
- Vendor lock-in concerns: engineering wants the option to run models in VPC/on-prem or on alternate clouds.
- Latency spikes during peak traffic affecting live chat SLAs (~95th pctl target ~<200ms for short-turn interactions).
- Compliance: need SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and strict data retention controls.

Current stack (as stated on the call):
- Production chat: OpenAI (gpt-4o family) for user-facing sessions, Anthropic Claude for some assistant flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings for search + similarity.
- Orchestration: homegrown queue + a thin abstraction around provider APIs.
- Volume: roughly 1.2M requests / month across chat + embeddings (you mentioned ~1.2B tokens/mo).

Success criteria for migration / PoC:
- Output parity: user-visible behavior within acceptable tolerance (we agreed to define a small eval set).
- Cost target: at least ~30–40% unit-cost reduction vs current spend (goal to justify migration).
- Latency: 95th pctl at or below ~200ms for short-turn chat (with autoscaling).
- Security & compliance: SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, and ability to use your KMS.

Compatibility notes we captured:
- Function/tool-calling: your front-end uses structured tool-calls; we may need a compatibility shim for some open models.
- Embedding dimensions / vector store: must match or be convertible to your vector DB without full reindexing if possible.

Next steps / owners:
1) Redwood to share a short model compatibility shortlist + SRE/SE availability for a deep dive — Rishi (internal) will own the deep technical deck. (ETA: Mon/Tue next week)
2) BrightDesk to share SOC2 / security questionnaire and any RFP docs — Samir to attach. (Done — please see your email thread)
3) Agree on an eval prompt set and measurement rubric for output parity — Marissa + Samir to align. (ETA: propose by EOD Mon)
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/SRE team to review latency/throughput and deployment options — Rishi to propose times.

Attachments referenced on call: BrightDesk RFP/security PDF (Samir mentioned sending) — please reply-all when you upload so we can add to the record.

Proposed PoC timeline (high-level):
- Week 0: Kickoff + access / security review
- Weeks 1–2: Baseline eval + model shortlist testing (small eval set)
- Weeks 3–4: PoC on dedicated capacity (latency + cost measurement)

Thanks again — happy to hop on another quick sync if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the RFP. I pulled together an initial compatibility and model shortlist for the PoC; attaching the spreadsheet with model notes (latency expectations, quantization feasibility, embedding dims, and rough cost estimates). High-level notes below so you have context before the deep dive.

Initial model shortlist (for PoC):
- Llama 2 Chat 70B (quantized runs look promising; strong chat quality for instruction-heavy flows)
- Mistral Large / Instruct variants (good instruction following with lower token cost)
- RedPajama-Chat / Falcon-based variants (smaller memory footprint; good for embeddings parity tests)
- MosaicML MPT-Chat / MPT-7B-Instruct (fast inference on A100/H100 with optimized kernels)

Compatibility considerations:
- Function-calling: we'll prototype a lightweight shim that maps your existing function-call schema to model-specific prompts + structured outputs. This preserves front-end contracts for the first pass.
- Embedding dimensions: aim to test RedPajama/Falcon variants for 1536-dim parity or use a conversion layer if dims differ (reindexing cost vs on-the-fly conversion tradeoff).
- Latency: with int8 quantization and batching tuned we expect sub-200ms p95 for short-turn models on dedicated A100/H100 pools for the smaller/medium models; larger 70B class will be closer but still feasible with optimized kernels and KV caching.

Next actions from Redwood SEs:
- Attach spreadsheet: redwood_model_compatibility_shortlist.xlsx (contains test plan + rough perf numbers).
- Propose Tue 30 Jun 10:00 PT for a technical deep-dive with infra/SRE. Rishi will lead and bring our runtime architect (Neha).

If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite with a focused agenda (latency targets, deployment topology, security onboarding checklist).

Thanks — look forward to the deep dive.
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
